name: Roman Empire
description: Ancient Roman civilization centered on the Mediterranean

name: Ancient Greece
description: Collection of Greek city-states in classical antiquity

name: Sumer
description: The earliest known civilization in southern Mesopotamia, credited with the invention of writing, the wheel, and early urban society

name: Akkadian Empire
description: First empire in Mesopotamia, uniting Sumerian and Akkadian-speaking peoples under Sargon of Akkad

name: Babylonian Empire
description: Mesopotamian civilization centered on Babylon, known for Hammurabi's code of laws and advances in astronomy and mathematics

name: Assyrian Empire
description: Powerful Mesopotamian empire known for its military prowess, vast library at Nineveh, and monumental architecture

name: Ancient Egypt
description: One of the longest-lasting civilizations in history, known for pyramids, pharaohs, and advances in writing, medicine, and architecture

name: Persian Empire (Achaemenid)
description: The largest empire of the ancient world, spanning from Egypt to India, known for its tolerance, infrastructure, and administrative innovation

name: Maurya Empire
description: First empire to unify most of the Indian subcontinent, known for Emperor Ashoka's promotion of Buddhism and nonviolence

name: Gupta Empire
description: Golden age of India marked by extraordinary achievements in science, mathematics, astronomy, art, and literature

name: Han Dynasty
description: One of China's golden ages, establishing the Silk Road, civil service examinations, and Confucianism as state ideology

name: Tang Dynasty
description: Widely regarded as a high point in Chinese civilization and a golden age of cosmopolitan culture, poetry, and trade

name: Mongol Empire
sources: ["The Secret History of the Mongols","Historical records"]
description: Largest contiguous land empire in history, founded by Genghis Khan, connecting East and West through trade and conquest

name: Ottoman Empire
description: Multi-ethnic empire spanning Southeast Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa for over six centuries

name: Byzantine Empire
description: Eastern continuation of the Roman Empire, preserving Greek culture, Roman law, and Orthodox Christianity for over a millennium

name: Holy Roman Empire
description: Complex multi-ethnic political entity in Central Europe, serving as the political framework for German-speaking lands for a millennium

name: Aztec Empire
description: Mesoamerican civilization known for its monumental architecture, complex calendar systems, and advanced agricultural techniques

name: Inca Empire
description: Largest empire in pre-Columbian America, renowned for its road system, terraced agriculture, and administrative sophistication

name: Maya Civilization
description: Mesoamerican civilization known for its advanced writing system, astronomical knowledge, mathematical concepts, and monumental architecture

name: Khmer Empire
native_name: ចក្រភពខ្មែរ
description: Southeast Asian empire centered on Angkor, builders of the largest religious monument in the world, Angkor Wat

name: Mali Empire
description: Wealthy West African empire known for Mansa Musa's legendary pilgrimage and the great center of learning at Timbuktu

name: Songhai Empire
description: Largest empire in African history, succeeding Mali, with Timbuktu as a major intellectual and trade center

name: Great Zimbabwe
description: Medieval African kingdom known for its massive stone enclosures, long-distance trade networks, and cattle-based economy

name: Carthage
description: Powerful maritime civilization in North Africa, major rival of Rome in the Punic Wars

name: Phoenicia
description: Maritime trading civilization that invented the alphabet, established colonies across the Mediterranean including Carthage

name: Indus Valley Civilization
description: One of the earliest urban civilizations, known for advanced city planning, drainage systems, and standardized weights and measures

name: Shang Dynasty
description: Earliest archaeologically verified Chinese dynasty, known for bronze casting, oracle bone divination, and early Chinese writing

name: Hittite Empire
description: Anatolian empire that rivaled Egypt, known for early iron use, diplomatic treaties, and one of the earliest known Indo-European languages

name: Umayyad Caliphate
description: Second of the four major caliphates, expanding the Islamic world from Spain to Central Asia and establishing Arabic as the administrative language

name: Abbasid Caliphate
description: Islamic Golden Age caliphate centered on Baghdad, fostering major advances in science, medicine, mathematics, and philosophy

name: Viking Territories
description: Norse seafaring peoples who explored, traded, and raided across Europe, the North Atlantic, and beyond

name: Celtic Territories
description: Diverse group of tribal societies across Europe known for distinctive art, metalwork, and oral traditions

name: Mughal Empire
description: Islamic empire in the Indian subcontinent known for cultural synthesis, architectural masterpieces like the Taj Mahal, and administrative reforms

name: Sasanian Empire
description: Last pre-Islamic Persian empire, known for its cultural and artistic achievements, Zoroastrian state religion, and rivalry with Rome and Byzantium
